classification.difficultyReason: Apply chord properties, equal radii and triangle angle sums across nine diagrams.

content.prompt: Find the size of each unknown value.

spec.description: Two radii and their chord; external arrow identifies the 20° base angle.
spec.mathematics: The radii form an isosceles triangle. The unknown is its interior central angle.

answer.worked:
The radii are equal, so both base angles are $20^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}a&=180^\circ-20^\circ-20^\circ\\a&=140^\circ\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Isosceles triangle formed by two radii and a chord, with the reflex central angle marked.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Minor central angle}&=360^\circ-260^\circ\\&=100^\circ\\a&=\frac{180^\circ-100^\circ}{2}\\a&=40^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The base angles are equal because the radii are equal.

spec.description: Centre joined to both chord endpoints and its midpoint; matching double ticks identify equal chord halves. No given right-angle mark.
spec.mathematics: The centre-to-midpoint segment is perpendicular to the chord; equal radii give equal endpoint angles.
spec.answerVisibility: 71° and a° are visible; no derived angle is supplied.

answer.worked:
The line from the centre to the midpoint of the chord is perpendicular to the chord.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Left endpoint angle}&=180^\circ-90^\circ-71^\circ\\&=19^\circ\\a&=19^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The endpoint angles are equal because the radii are equal.

spec.description: Diameter from upper-left to bottom, third vertex upper-right, and additional radius to that vertex.
spec.mathematics: The centre and two lower triangle vertices form an isosceles triangle. The upper central angle is supplementary to its central angle.

answer.worked:
The two radii to the bottom and upper-right points are equal.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Lower central angle}&=180^\circ-2(18^\circ)\\&=144^\circ\\\text{Upper central angle}&=180^\circ-144^\circ\\&=36^\circ\\a&=\frac{180^\circ-36^\circ}{2}\\a&=72^\circ\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Diameter, two chords to an upper-left vertex and its radius; double ticks match one chord to a radius.
spec.mathematics: The left triangle is equilateral. The remaining central angle is 120°, giving equal base angles of 30°.
spec.answerVisibility: Only a° and the supplied equality marks are visible.

answer.worked:
The marked chord and both radii of the left triangle are equal, so it is equilateral.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Right central angle}&=180^\circ-60^\circ\\&=120^\circ\\a&=\frac{180^\circ-120^\circ}{2}\\a&=30^\circ\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Five equal chords form an inscribed pentagon; all five vertices are joined to the centre.
spec.mathematics: Equal chords subtend five equal central angles. Each corresponding triangle is isosceles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only a° and matching double ticks are visible.

answer.worked:
Equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Each central angle}&=\frac{360^\circ}{5}\\&=72^\circ\\a&=\frac{180^\circ-72^\circ}{2}\\a&=54^\circ\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Left and right chords subtend separately labelled 20° angles at centre O.
spec.mathematics: Chords subtending equal central angles are equal; the schematic proportions are not measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: Both 20° labels, 30 cm, x and O are visible.

answer.worked: $x=30\text{ cm}$, because chords subtending equal angles at the centre are equal.

spec.description: Six successive chords and three diameters; labels x, y, 4 cm, 6 cm, 5 cm and z follow clockwise order.
spec.mathematics: Vertically opposite central angles are equal, so the corresponding opposite chords are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: All given chord lengths and unknown labels are visible; answers are omitted.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite angles at $O$ are equal. Chords subtending equal central angles are equal.
$$\begin{aligned}x&=6\text{ cm}\\y&=5\text{ cm}\\z&=4\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Two equal chords, each labelled 3 cm, with perpendicular distances from centre O labelled 5 cm and x.
spec.mathematics: Equal chords are equidistant from the centre; right-angle squares are derived from the perpendicular directions.
spec.answerVisibility: 3 cm twice, 5 cm, x and O are visible.

answer.worked: $x=5\text{ cm}$, because equal chords are equidistant from the centre.
